subject: Data Engineering
title: What Is a Message Broker?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Is a Message Broker?.

hook.text: Two services need to share data without talking directly to each other. A broker sits in the middle.

buildup.text: A message broker receives events from producers, stores them temporarily, and delivers them to consumers.

discovery.text: Brokers decouple senders from receivers, buffer traffic spikes, and enable reliable async communication.

twist.text: Without a broker, every service must know every other service's address. That creates a fragile web.

climax.text: Brokers are the postal service of streaming — they route events so services don't have to.

punchline.text: Don't connect everything to everything. Use a broker.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of a message broker?
options: Decoupling producers and consumers with reliable delivery
